View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; getAddPaxOfferId/getAddPaxResponceID available. Collection variables reset before starting (SPEC.md §6.1).
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (send ResponseId/selectedOfferId = AddPassenger's IDs) -> capture resp.offerId/resp.responseId -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId).
Expected Result
GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a non-empty offerId/responseId; the collection variables getSeatMapOfferId and getSeatMapResponceID (note the collection's own "Responce" spelling) are populated from these; Book accepts them and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without needing AddPassenger's IDs re-sent -- this is a behavior change from before 2026-08-10, when GetSeatMap set no variables at all and Book still read AddPassenger's IDs.
Actual Result
Confirmed. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (identical to the AddPassenger values); Book accepted them and created a real ticketed PNR. The Postman collection-variable assignment itself is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP - verified the field mapping it relies on (resp.offerId/resp.responseId) instead. BUG-16 (Book 409 with a silently created booking, Round 12) did NOT reproduce on this call: a clean 200 with a PNR. Unchanged from Rounds 1-11.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; a cellCode/cellId recorded for an AvailablePaid cell; the pnr's bookingStatus/ticketStatus (per Retrieve) confirmed not yet ticketed before this check is made.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats) -> Retrieve immediately afterward, with no ticketing action taken in between -> inspect bookingStatus/ticketStatus alongside the seat-related fields.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: the immediate post-Book Retrieve already shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated with the selected seat, while bookingStatus/ticketStatus still reads as un-ticketed/un-issued (e.g. Booked, not Ticketed). This confirms the seat is attached to the reservation at Book time and does not depend on a later payment/ticketing step existing or completing. If bookingStatus already reads as ticketed/paid immediately post-Book with no intervening action taken, record that as a finding rather than assuming the AC's ordering holds.
Actual Result
The seat is attached at Book time: Retrieve, taken right after Book with no other action, shows passengersSelectedSeats, passengerSeats and totalSelectedSeatsAmount populated. GulfAir tickets synchronously at Book (a ticket number and ticketingDate exist immediately), so there is no un-ticketed window to isolate - the same caveat as every prior round. The core assertion holds.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed; at least one Blocked or Occupied cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a Blocked/Occupied cell) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats using that cell's cellCode/cellId).
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no booking is created, or if a PNR is created it must NOT reflect the unavailable seat as attached -- either outcome should be logged precisely, since both are plausible failure modes for an unenforced availability check.
Actual Result
Both outcomes the test allows, and no unavailable seat was ever attached. Run 1 (the real null cellId of an unavailable cell) is rejected by a generic null-cellId check, not by an availability check. Run 2 (unavailable code + a borrowed valid token) is NOT rejected: Book created and ticketed a booking and silently left the seat out (passengersSelectedSeats {}), with no error telling the caller the seat was dropped - the same silent-drop pattern as BUG-07. Blocked/Occupied cells do not exist for this supplier, so NoSeat is the closest unavailable state.
TC-BOOK-NEG-06 - Validate Book rejects a passengersSelectedSeats.cellId value that has been truncated or otherwise tampered with.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check booking refuses a tampered seat code
Request: Booked seat 14A (Bahrain to Dubai, 17 June) but changed the last 10 characters of its seat code
Response: Booking accepted and ticketed (reference RALBKE); seat 14A attached at 60 SAR as if nothing was wrong
Expected: The tampered seat code should be refused
Actual: BUG-06, 7th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the seat code is never checked; the seat is chosen from the short code alone
Status: FAIL
Evidence
tampered token length 323 (same as original), last 10 chars XXXXXXXXXX; Book 200; pnr RALBKE; passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 = {14A, 60 SAR}; total 1141 = 730 + 351 + 60

View Test Case
Preconditions
A Hold call completed long enough ago (or against a short-TTL test scenario) that holdExpirationDate is confirmed in the past via Retrieve.
Steps
  1. Hold -> wait until holdExpirationDate has passed (confirm via Retrieve) -> SeatAfterHold (submit the now-expired pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName).
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live), consistent with the same expectation already documented for FareConfirmAfterHold on an expired hold (§2.12).
Actual Result
Doubly blocked: no hold expiry is ever returned (BUG-04 reproduces on 3 fresh Holds, so there is no time to wait for), and SeatAfterHold rejects GulfAir outright (BUG-03). No call was made for this case beyond the Holds already shown.
TC-BOOK-NEG-07 - Validate Book rejects a request that assigns the same seat cell to two different passengers.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check the same seat cannot be given to two passengers
Request: Two adults (Bahrain to Cairo, 20 June 2027) both assigned seat 17C
Response: Refused in 0.1 seconds: "Seat 17C is assigned to multiple passengers"; no booking
Expected: Refused before anything is booked
Actual: Correct: a clear, immediate refusal naming the seat. It uses the general error code rather than a dedicated one
Status: PASS
Evidence
HTTP 400 in 0.1s; ErrorCode NDC-INT-TEC-A0001; Context: Seat '17C' is assigned to multiple passengers; no pnr in the response

Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with 2+ passengers; GetSeatMap completed and one AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId recorded.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record one cellCode/cellId) -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats.T1.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=that cell AND passengersSelectedSeats.T2.setSegmentsSeats.<seg>=the same cell).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: request rejected (candidate error code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST, per Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-009) before any supplier round-trip; exact status UNKNOWN-confirm-live. No pnr created.
Actual Result
Rejected cleanly and fast (0.1s, so before any supplier call) with a specific, on-point validation message naming the seat and segment. The candidate code DUPLICATE_SEAT_SELECTION_IN_REQUEST is not used - the envelope is the generic 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 with the message in Context. No booking was created. Unchanged from Rounds 5-6. (This is a different scenario from BUG-07, which is a cross-offer cellId.)
TC-BOOK-NEG-08 - Validate Book rejects a request where the same passenger selects two different seats on the same segment.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check what happens if the same segment appears twice for one passenger
Request: Hand-wrote a request that lists the same flight segment twice with seats 14C and 14D (Bahrain to Riyadh, 27 May 2027)
Response: Booking accepted and ticketed (reference OSEOSA) with only the second seat, 14D
Expected: Unknown — a normal request cannot even express this, so just record the behaviour
Actual: Documented: the last entry wins and the first seat is dropped without any error
Status: PASS
Evidence
raw body carried the segment key twice; response passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1.<segment> = {14D, 60 SAR}; seat 14C absent; total 1053

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed with 2+ AvailablePaid cells recorded for the same segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record two distinct cellCode/cellId pairs for the same segmentRefId) -> Book (attempt to submit both under the same passengersSelectedSeats.<pax>.setSegmentsSeats.<segmentRefId> key, or via whatever malformed-duplicate construction the request library allows).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- since setSegmentsSeats is keyed by segmentRefId (a JSON object, not an array), a client cannot literally submit two values under one key -- this case instead documents that constraint and verifies the last-value-wins/serialization behavior of the test client is understood, rather than asserting a specific API rejection.
Actual Result
Constraint documented and behavior observed: in valid JSON the segment key can appear only once, and when a raw body forces the duplicate the server keeps the LAST value (seat 14D) and drops the first (14C) without any error or warning. So two different seats on one segment for one passenger is impossible to express, and a client bug that repeats the key is silently resolved to the last entry.
TC-BOOK-NEG-09 - Validate graceful rollback (no orphaned PNR or charge) when the supplier's seat allocation call fails or times out after Book is submitted with a seat selection.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Check the booking cleans up if the airline fails to allocate the seat
Request: Tried to provoke a seat failure by asking for a seat code that does not exist (99Z) with a real seat code borrowed from another seat
Response: Booking accepted and ticketed (reference REPIRE) with no seat and no error
Expected: An error and no half-finished booking
Actual: Blocked: the failure cannot be forced from the request. The fake seat was simply dropped, which is another example of the BUG-07 pattern
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
Book 200; pnr REPIRE; passengersSelectedSeats {}; totalSelectedSeatsAmount 0; totalAmount 1143

View Test Case
Preconditions
A completed FareConfirm/AddPassenger chain for an offer confirmed (via the live capability flag, §2.2) to have isSeatMapRequired=false.
Steps
  1. FareConfirm/AddPassenger (confirm isSeatMapRequired=false on the live offer) -> GetSeatMap (call anyway, using that offer's IDs) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion once observed: rejected or an explicit unsupported-operation envelope is returned (candidate shape: the same {ErrorCode:'OperationNotSupported', ErrorMessage:...} envelope already confirmed live for GetOfferBundles on a haveBundles=false offer, §2.4) rather than a 200 with an empty/malformed seatMapDetails. Exact shape UNKNOWN for this specific endpoint -- confirm live and record.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-15). FareConfirm reports isSeatMapRequired=false (and haveBundles=false) on both offers, yet GetSeatMap returns HTTP 200 with a complete seat map on both. The flag is not enforced.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-02 - Validate GetSeatMap is rejected when the request otherwise targets a valid offer but no segment of that offer's itinerary is being queried (i.e., the offer/response pair does not correspond to any real segment).FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map refuses mismatched references
Request: Mixed the response reference from one offer with the offer reference from another (Bahrain to Riyadh and Bahrain to Jeddah), both ways round
Response: 200 both times; the seat map followed the offer reference and ignored the other
Expected: Refused
Actual: BUG-01, 7th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the pair is not cross-checked
Status: FAIL
Evidence
run 1 (respA+offerA2): 200, 28 rows (JED segment GF181); run 2 (respA2+offerA): 200, 30 rows (RUH segment GF161)

  1. AddPassenger for Offer A and Offer B separately -> GetSeatMap using Offer A's ResponseId but Offer B's selectedOfferId (or vice versa) -> observe response.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9); no seatMapDetails should be returned for a segment set that doesn't belong to the referenced offer.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-01). Both mismatched pairings were accepted with HTTP 200 and a full seat map; the result follows selectedOfferId and ResponseId is ignored.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-03 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects a stale or entirely invalid ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map refuses made-up or stale references
Request: Sent a made-up pair, and a real pair whose booking was already completed
Response: Made-up pair: refused (400). Already-booked pair: seat map returned (200)
Expected: Both refused
Actual: The made-up pair is refused cleanly. The already-booked pair still works, which is treated as harmless (a read-only look) as in earlier rounds, but it does not meet the literal expected result
Status: PASS
Evidence
run 1: 400 A0001 SelectedOfferId "Failed to deserialize the selected offer"; run 2: 200, 137 seat cells, pair already booked (pnr ONUNXZ)

View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond valid supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Run 1: GetSeatMap with a fabricated ResponseId/selectedOfferId. Run 2: GetSeatMap with a genuine but stale pair from a prior, since-superseded AddPassenger call in the same session.
Expected Result
Both runs rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live); no seatMapDetails returned for either.
Actual Result
Run 1 (a genuinely fabricated pair) is cleanly rejected with a structured 400. Run 2 is NOT rejected: a real pair keeps working after its offer has been booked - IDs are not invalidated by use. Recorded PASS on the established basis of Rounds 1-6 (the fabricated-pair rejection is the defect check; reading a seat map for an already-booked offer is idempotent and is not tracked as a defect), but note the literal expected result for run 2 is not met.
TC-SEATMAP-NEG-04 - Validate GetSeatMap rejects requests with each mandatory field individually omitted: supplier, credentialsSelector, ResponseId, selectedOfferId.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map refuses each missing required field
Request: Four requests, each missing one field: airline, credentials, response reference, offer reference
Response: Three refused with a clear message; missing response reference returned the full seat map
Expected: All four refused
Actual: BUG-02, 7th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the response reference is required but not checked (the returned reference is all zeros)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
omit supplier 400 "Select a valid Supplier"; omit credentialsSelector 400 "Select a valid CredentialsSelector"; omit selectedOfferId 400 "The SelectedOfferId field is required."; omit ResponseId 200 with 30 rows

View Test Case
Preconditions
A mechanism to force or simulate a supplier-side GetSeatMap failure is available (may not be reliably reproducible on every environment).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap targeting a scenario expected to fail at the supplier round-trip -> inspect the response body/status and any correlation-ID/tracing field present.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (once a forcing mechanism exists): response is a structured business-error envelope (matching this API's other confirmed error envelopes, e.g. §2.9's {Status,TransactionId,ErrorCode,ErrorMessage,Context} shape) rather than an unhandled exception/stack trace/raw supplier XML leak. No internal .NET type names or raw supplier payloads should leak into the error body (cross-ref the Context-leak defect already flagged at §2.9).
Actual Result
GetSeatMap's own error paths are graceful and structured. The half of the test that needs a real supplier failure could not be run for GetSeatMap, and the one natural supplier failure seen this round (on FareConfirm) does leak the raw upstream request and credentials in its envelope (BUG-11 re-confirmed) - so graceful supplier-failure handling is verified for the request-validation paths only. View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer; a specific AvailablePaid cell identified in the response.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> record cellDetails.cellID (capital ID) for a chosen AvailablePaid cell, plus its cellCode -> Book (submit passengersSelectedSeats with cellCode and cellId=<the recorded cellID value>).
Expected Result
Book accepts the token despite the field-name casing difference between the response (cellID) and the request (cellId) and attaches the correct seat, echoed back in the response's passengersSelectedSeats/selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats.
Actual Result
Accepted. The request sent the response's cellID value verbatim under the lowercase-d field name cellId; Book returned 200, attached seat 12C and echoed it at three places (top-level passengersSelectedSeats, selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown[].passengerSeats, priceDetails.totalSelectedSeats). The casing difference is cosmetic (case-insensitive JSON binding). Unchanged from Rounds 1-11. BUG-16 did not reproduce on this call.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-04 - Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check a seat code from one offer is refused on a different offer
Request: Opened seat maps for two different offers (Bahrain to Jeddah, 15 and 16 June), then booked on the second offer with seat 15B but the seat code that belongs to seat 15C on the first offer
Response: Booking accepted and ticketed (reference RFMLTX); the seat was silently left out, with no error
Expected: The booking should be refused straight away because the seat code belongs to another offer
Actual: BUG-07, 9th confirmed occurrence (not new) — the foreign seat code was not rejected. A ticket was issued and the customer is left with no seat and no warning
Status: FAIL

Book 200 in 37.1s; pnr RFMLTX, ticket 722136997201; passengersSelectedSeats {} ; priceDetails totalAmount 1143 = base 790 + tax 353, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 0

View Test Case
Preconditions
Two independent, completed Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap chains (Offer A and Offer B) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, record cellID_A. Chain B: Search->FareConfirm->AddPassenger->GetSeatMap, obtain getSeatMapResponceID_B/getSeatMapOfferId_B. Book using Chain B's ResponseId/selectedOfferId but passengersSelectedSeats.cellId=cellID_A.
Expected Result
Request is rejected (exact status UNKNOWN -- confirm live per §7.9), since cellID appears (per its base64-decoded contents) to embed the originating ResponseId/OfferId/passenger-ref metadata and is presumably bound to the offer it was issued for.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-07). The foreign cellId was not rejected: Book ran the full supplier round-trip, created and ticketed a real booking, and silently dropped the seat (passengersSelectedSeats {} and no seat fee) instead of returning an error. Seat 15B was neither attached nor refused.
TC-BOOK-VAL-06 - Validate Book's behavior when passengersSelectedSeats.cellCode does not match the cell that cellId actually encodes.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check what happens when the short seat code and the long seat code point to different seats
Request: Booked with short code 15F but the long code that belongs to seat 15A (Bahrain to Jeddah, 18 June)
Response: Booking accepted and ticketed (reference OWBPFD); seat 15F was attached
Expected: Unknown — the system might trust either code, refuse, or book the wrong seat
Actual: Answer found: the system trusts the short code and ignores the long one, with no cross-check (the same weakness as BUG-06)
Status: FAIL
Evidence
Book 200; pnr OWBPFD; passengersSelectedSeats.PAX1 = {15F, 60 SAR}; seat 15A (the token's seat) not attached; total 1203 = 790 + 353 + 60

Preconditions
AddPassenger and GetSeatMap completed; two distinct AvailablePaid cellCode/cellId pairs recorded (cell A and cell B).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (record cell A and cell B) -> construct a Book request with passengersSelectedSeats=cell A -> before sending, replace passengersSelectedSeats with cell B -> send the single Book request (cell A is never actually transmitted).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds and reflects cell B only -- passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats show cell B's cellCode/price; cell A does not appear anywhere in the response, and cell A's availability (per a follow-up GetSeatMap, if re-queryable) is unaffected by the abandoned selection.
Actual Result
The single Book call carried cell 12C and the response reflects only 12C at every location (60.00 SAR); no other cell code appears. This is a client-side construction check: only one Book is ever sent, so there is no cached/earlier selection to leak. Every Book sent this round is checked the same way.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell's cellCharacteristics[], pair padisCode with description -> check each pair against a maintained reference mapping (e.g. A=Aisle, W=Window, E=Exit seat, per the QC checklist's simplified mapping) -- note SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3 itself has observed a wider code set (CH, _8, _9, _14, K, LS, OW, RS, V, FC, Unknown) not covered by the checklist's simplified 5-code table.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for every padisCode value observed, description must not contradict the code's known meaning per the now-sourced canonical reference table. Codes still outside that table should be rare -- log any such pairing rather than asserting pass/fail.
Actual Result
GulfAir's adapter never populates a real padisCode (780 of 780 are "Unknown"), so no code can contradict its description; the description strings are self-describing enums (CHARGEABLE_SEAT, FRONT_OF_CABIN, WINDOW, LEFT/RIGHT_SIDE_OF_AIRCRAFT, CENTER_SEAT, AISLE_SEAT, OVER_WING_SEAT_S, EXIT_ROW_SEAT, PREFERRED_SEAT_PREFERENTIAL_SEAT, LEG_SPACE_SEAT). Logged, not failed. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one Aisle-category cell present.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, branch on cellCategory -> if Aisle, assert column and cellDetails; if Seat, assert column and cellDetails.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: cellCategory=Aisle implies column is null AND cellDetails is null; cellCategory=Seat implies column is non-null AND cellDetails is a populated object (per TC-SEATMAP-REG-02's field list). No cell violates this partition.
Actual Result
0 violations. All 30 Aisle cells have column null and cellDetails null; all 174 Seat cells have a letter column (A-F) and a populated cellDetails object. The 6 NoSeat cells (row 8) have a real column letter and cellDetails null - outside this rule, noted only.

Expected: Attributes derivable and not contradicting the seat's position
Actual: All 174 consistent, but only through the description text (the standard codes are all "Unknown")
Status: PASS

column/description mismatches 0 of 174; WINDOW 58, AISLE_SEAT 58, CENTER_SEAT 58; EXIT_ROW_SEAT 24 (rows 18-21); LEG_SPACE 12; OVER_WING 48; padisCode Unknown 780/780

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails covering a mix of window/aisle/middle/exit-row seats.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every Seat-category cell, read cellCharacteristics[].padisCode -> classify each cell as window/aisle/extra-legroom/other using the reference table -> spot-check against the cell's own column position (e.g. the outermost column of a zone should carry a window-adjacent code) and description text.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: for codes present in the now-sourced canonical reference table (NDC_Integration/Resources/SeatResources/PadisSeatCharacteristic.md), the derived classification must not contradict column position or description text. Codes outside that table are logged, not failed.
Actual Result
Every Seat cell's description carries a window/aisle/centre marker and a left/right-side marker, and 0 of 174 contradict the cell's column (A/F=WINDOW, C/D=AISLE_SEAT, B/E=CENTER_SEAT; A-C=LEFT, D-F=RIGHT). Extra legroom (LEG_SPACE_SEAT, 12 cells) and exit row (EXIT_ROW_SEAT, 24 cells, rows 18-21) are derivable from the text too. padisCode is "Unknown" everywhere, so the attributes are only derivable from description text (logged, not failed). Unchanged from Rounds 1-12.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-08 - Verify seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is populated (non-null) for every AvailablePaid cell and null/absent for every Blocked or Occupied cell.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check only bookable seats carry prices
Request: Grouped every seat of the seat maps by availability
Response: Every bookable seat has a full price; no other cell has any price
Expected: Bookable seats priced; unavailable ones not
Actual: Confirmed. The "blocked/occupied" half cannot be exercised because this airline hides taken seats
Status: PASS

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed with a populated seatMapDetails containing a mix of AvailablePaid, Blocked, and Occupied cells.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every cell, read cellAvailability and cellDetails.seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger -> group by availability value.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every AvailablePaid cell has a non-null seatPriceDetailsByPassenger with populated totalPrice/basePrice/taxesPrice per passenger (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-02's reconciliation); every Blocked/Occupied cell has seatPriceDetails null (consistent with SPEC.md §2.7's observed example, which shows seatPriceDetails: null on a Blocked cell).
Actual Result
AvailablePaid: every one of the ~6,470 seat cells has seatPriceDetailsByPassenger with totalPrice, basePrice and taxesPrice populated. The Blocked/Occupied half could not be exercised - no Blocked or Occupied cell exists for this supplier (taken seats appear as NoSeat with null cellDetails, so no pricing). No non-paid cell carries pricing (0 violations). The aggregate seatPriceDetails is null on every cell.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for one segment, collect every rowNumber (check uniqueness), every zoneId per deck (check uniqueness within that deck), and every cell's column value (check domain membership).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: no rowNumber repeats within the segment; no zoneId repeats within the same deck; every non-null column value is one of A/B/C/D/E/F (per the observed 6-column-per-row layout, SPEC.md §2.7); null column values correspond only to Aisle-category cells (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-VAL-06).
Actual Result
All four constraints hold: 30 row numbers, 30 unique; 1 zone in deck Main; Seat-cell columns are exactly {A,B,C,D,E,F}; the 30 null-column cells are all Aisle-category. Every row's deck/zoneId resolves to the declared layout.
TC-SEATMAP-VAL-11 - Verify passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the top-level per-passenger allow-list of cellCodes) stays internally consistent with per-cell seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries, and verify segment-ref keys are used with consistent casing throughout the response.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check the per-passenger seat lists are consistent
Request: Read the passenger seat list of one seat map and compared it with the flight and seat data
Response: The list uses the exact flight key and holds 174 seats, all real
Expected: Keys match in casing; every listed seat exists
Actual: Confirmed, and every bookable seat is on the list
Status: PASS
Evidence
allow-list segment keys=1 (identical casing); deck keys [Main]; allow-list length 174; codes not present as cells=0; paid cells missing from allow-list=0

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment offer with a populated passengersSeatMapAvailability block.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every passenger, read passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> -> confirm every key is a segmentRefId that also appears in flightSegments/seatMapDetails using EXACTLY the same casing -> for a sample of cellCode values in each passenger's allow-list, confirm that cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger (if priced) includes that passenger when the passenger is expected to be priced there.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: (1) every segmentRefId key under passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef> matches the casing used elsewhere in the same response (flightSegments/seatMapDetails keys) -- a differently-cased key for the same logical segment (e.g. "Seg3" vs "SEG1"/"SEG2") is a confirmed defect, not an acceptable variation; (2) every cellCode listed in a passenger's allow-list corresponds to a real cell in that segment's seatMapDetails.
Actual Result
The allow-list key is the full segmentRefId and matches the seatMapDetails/flightSegments key character-for-character; all 174 allow-listed codes exist as real cells and every AvailablePaid cell is on the list (0 missing). The block is nested one level deeper than SPEC.md describes (segment -> deck "Main" -> cellCode array). No casing inconsistency for GulfAir.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> enumerate every cells[] entry across all rows for one segment -> record the distinct cellCategory and cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability values observed.
Expected Result
Every cellCategory value observed is one of {Seat, Aisle}; every cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value observed is one of {AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied}. If a new value appears (e.g. an "available free" state), log it and flag rather than hard-failing (§8.3 policy for UNKNOWN enumerations) -- do not assume the three known values are exhaustive.
Actual Result
No Blocked or Occupied value appeared anywhere. Two values outside the expected sets were found and are flagged, not failed (8.3 policy): cellCategory "NoSeat" (a taken/absent seat, cellDetails null) and paxCellAvailability "AvailableFree" (seat 8E, the bassinet seat, on the A320 GF103 flights: overall cellAvailability stays AvailablePaid while every passenger entry says AvailableFree at 0.00 SAR - 6 passenger entries across 5 maps). Every Aisle cell has cellDetails null, so no price.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger, multi-segment itinerary; at least two distinct AvailablePaid cells recorded.
Steps
  1. Run (a): Book with passengersSelectedSeats omitted. Run (b): Book with one paxRef/one segmentRefId as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. Run (c): Book with two paxRef keys, each containing a setSegmentsSeats map with two segmentRefId entries.
Expected Result
(a) Book succeeds with no seat attached (passengersSelectedSeats absent/empty in the response). (b) succeeds as in TC-BOOK-POS-03. (c) UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether multiple passengers/segments nest correctly as sibling keys per SPEC.md §2.9's schema description, since only the single-passenger/single-segment shape has a directly-observed example.
Actual Result
All three sub-cases pass. (c) is now directly evidenced: two passenger keys, each with a setSegmentsSeats map of two segment keys, are accepted and echoed correctly at every location, and the totals reconcile (base 1698 + tax 1522 + seats 200 = 3420.00 SAR; each passenger paxTotalSeatAmount 100 = 60 + 40 on the Book response). The multi-seat Retrieve of the same bookings under-reports the per-passenger seat total - filed separately under FLOW-V2-49-SEATFIELD (BUG-18).
TC-SEATMAP-BND-03 - Verify AvailableFree is accepted as a real cellAvailability value (confirmed via saved example) and confirm live whether AvailableAfterReservation is also real, beyond the four now-evidenced values (AvailablePaid, Blocked, Occupied, AvailableFree).PASS
Endpoint Name: Check which "free seat" values exist

Response: One free bassinet seat (8E on the A320 flights to Dammam) is "free" for each passenger at 0 SAR, while the seat itself still counts as "for a fee"
Expected: The "free" value is real; the "available after reservation" value is unconfirmed
Actual: New live proof that "free" exists for this airline too, at passenger level with an explicit 0 SAR price. "Available after reservation" was never seen
Status: PASS
Evidence
GF103 (equipment 320) maps: 8E paxCellAvailability AvailableFree x6 entries, totalPrice 0 SAR; overall cellAvailability AvailablePaid; no cell anywhere shows AvailableAfterReservation

Large arrays, objects and long opaque tokens are truncated for report length (marked "__omitted__" / "[truncated]"); the full payload was inspected live. Raw supplier payloads are redacted per SPEC.md §7.14.
View Test Case
Preconditions
None beyond a completed GetSeatMap call; deliberately sample several suppliers/fare classes known to include free-seat-selection fare products (e.g. Ultimate/Premium bundle tiers per §2.4's bundle rule descriptions mentioning free seat rows).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/offers, prioritizing fare classes whose priceClasses.rulesAndPenalties mention seat-related perks (e.g. §2.4's observed "Seat: row 8 onwards" / "Seat: Row 3 onwards" bundle rules) -> scan every cell's cellAvailability/paxCellAvailability value -> assert AvailableFree cells have seatPriceDetails/seatPriceDetailsByPassenger null (matching the confirmed example), and continue sampling specifically for AvailableAfterReservation.
Expected Result
CONFIRMED live for AvailableFree as of 2026-08-24 (see saved example above) -- update SPEC.md §2.7/§8.3's enum list to add AvailableFree to the observed set. AvailableAfterReservation remains UNKNOWN; if found, add with evidence, if never observed after a reasonably broad sample, record it as an unconfirmed QC-checklist-only candidate rather than promoting it.
Actual Result
New live evidence: AvailableFree is a real value on GulfAir too, at the per-passenger level (8E, the bassinet seat, on all 5 GF103 maps sampled, 6 passenger entries). It differs from the saved AirArabia example in one respect: the AirArabia AvailableFree cells carry null pricing, whereas GulfAir returns explicit 0.00 SAR price objects (total = base + taxes = 0) and keeps the overall cellAvailability at AvailablePaid. AvailableAfterReservation was not observed in any of the 34 segments and stays an unconfirmed candidate.
TC-SEATMAP-BND-04 - Confirm live whether any cellCategory value beyond {Seat, Aisle} (e.g. Lavatory/Bathroom, Bulkhead, Galley, Closet, ExitRow, StairsToUpperDeck, WingBox, StorageBin, RestrictedZone, NoSeat, Other, per the full backend enum) is ever returned.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check which seat categories exist beyond seat and aisle
Request: Scanned every cell of 34 flights on four narrowbody aircraft types
Response: Only seat, aisle and "no seat" appear
Expected: Record every category seen
Actual: One extra category, "no seat" (a taken or missing seat). No toilets, galleys or upper decks appear on these aircraft, so the naming question stays open
Status: PASS
Evidence
distinct cellCategory values across ~7,000 cells: Seat, Aisle, NoSeat; equipment 320, 321, 32N, 32Q; decks: Main only

View Test Case
Preconditions
A broad sample of GetSeatMap responses across suppliers/aircraft types (widebody aircraft with galleys/bulkheads/stairs-to-upper-deck are the most likely candidates for the rarer members).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap across several suppliers/aircraft (prioritize widebody/double-decker equipment) -> scan every cells[].cellCategory value -> record every distinct value observed, comparing against BOTH CellCategory.md's enum names and the raw example's own comment naming.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Only Seat and Aisle are confirmed as of 2026-08-24; every other member (including whichever name -- Lavatory or Bathroom -- the bathroom-equivalent category actually uses live) remains unconfirmed. Do not assume Seat/Aisle are exhaustive, and do not assume the C# enum's member names match what the API actually serializes (the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming discrepancy between the raw example's comment and the enum source must be resolved live, not guessed).
Actual Result
Beyond Seat and Aisle, only "NoSeat" was observed (a taken or absent seat; cellDetails null; matches CellCategory.md's NoSeat member). No Lavatory/Bathroom/Galley/Bulkhead/ExitRow/StairsToUpperDeck category appeared, and no widebody or double-deck aircraft is available to GulfAir/KSA in this sample, so the Lavatory-vs-Bathroom naming question stays unresolved.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer with at least one AvailablePaid cell.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for every AvailablePaid cell, read seatPriceDetailsByPassenger.<paxRef>.{totalPrice, basePrice, taxesPrice}.
Expected Result
totalPrice.amount == basePrice.amount + taxesPrice.amount for every priced cell/passenger pair, in the same currency; no cell reports a totalPrice inconsistent with its own basePrice+taxesPrice.
Actual Result
0 mismatches in 7,060 pairs. basePrice equals totalPrice everywhere and taxesPrice is 0.00 SAR (GulfAir does not split a seat charge into base and tax); the free bassinet seat 8E is 0 = 0 + 0. All amounts are in SAR.
TC-BOOK-BIZ-04 - Verify selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalAmount includes totalSelectedSeatsAmount when a seat has been selected.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check the seat fee is included in the booking total
Request: Booked one seat (12C, 60 SAR) and compared the total with the fare quoted before the seat was added
Response: Total 993 SAR = fare 580 + tax 353 + seat 60; the earlier quote was 933 SAR
Expected: Total equals fare plus tax plus seats, and equals the earlier total plus the seat
Actual: Both checks add up exactly
Status: PASS
Evidence
totalBase 580 + totalTax 353 + totalAnc 0 + totalSeats 60 = 993 == totalAmount 993; FareConfirm totalAmount 933 + seat 60 = 993

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-BOOK-POS-03 completed and its response captured; the same offer's pre-seat FareConfirm/AddPassenger-era totalAmount also captured.
Steps
  1. Book (with passengersSelectedSeats populated) -> read selectedOffer.priceDetails.{totalAmount, totalBaseAmount, totalTaxAmount, totalAncillariesAmount, totalSelectedSeatsAmount} -> compare totalAmount against totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and against the pre-seat-selection totalAmount plus the seat's price.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expected (per the existing price-reconciliation formula's pattern, §2.1) is totalAmount == totalBaseAmount + totalTaxAmount + totalAncillariesAmount + totalSelectedSeatsAmount, and totalAmount(after) == totalAmount(before seat selection) + totalSelectedSeatsAmount. Neither V1 nor V2's existing price-reconciliation test scripts were observed summing a seat amount, so this is unverified either way -- treat any mismatch as a confirmed defect, not an UNKNOWN to shrug off, once run.
Actual Result
Both reconcile exactly: 580.00 + 353.00 + 0.00 + 60.00 = 993.00 = totalAmount, and 933.00 (FareConfirm) + 60.00 = 993.00. The seat amount is included in totalAmount. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.
TC-BOOK-BIZ-05 - Validate a Child (CHD) passenger assigned an Exit Row seat is rejected server-side.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check a child cannot be given an exit-row seat

Expected: Refused, and no booking created
Actual: BUG-09, 9th confirmed occurrence (not new) — nothing stops a child being seated in an exit row. The seat map even offers all 24 exit-row seats to the child
Status: FAIL
Evidence
CHD PAX2 allow-list contains 10A (24 of 24 exit-row cells offered); Book 200; pnr OODUCQ; passengersSelectedSeats.PAX2 = {10A, 60 SAR}; total 2655 = base 1829 + tax 706 + seats 120

Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with at least one CHD passenger; GetSeatMap completed and an exit-row cell (cellCharacteristics containing an Exit-seat characteristic) identified for that passenger's segment.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (CHD present) -> GetSeatMap (identify an exit-row cellCode/cellId via cellCharacteristics) -> Book (assign that cellCode/cellId to the CHD passenger's setSegmentsSeats entry, bypassing any client-side UI restriction).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: response status is an error (candidate error code RESTRICTED_EXIT_ROW_SEAT_FOR_CHILD, per this suite's Seat map - Seatmap.md TC-INT-BOOK-008 reference) and no pnr is created for this attempt. Candidate code is UNKNOWN-confirm-live -- not yet observed in any Postman-collection saved example; record the exact code/status returned and update this row plus SPEC.md §2.9 once confirmed.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES in its worsened form (BUG-09). GetSeatMap itself lists the exit-row cell 10A in the CHD passenger's allow-list and prices it for the CHD; Book then accepts the CHD in an exit-row seat with zero validation, creates the PNR and tickets both passengers. No child/exit-row restriction exists anywhere in the flow.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed with one ADT + one INF (parentPaxRefId linking them, §2.5); GetSeatMap completed; a seat selected only for the ADT.
Steps
  1. AddPassenger (ADT+INF) -> GetSeatMap -> Book (passengersSelectedSeats contains only the ADT's paxRef; INF's paxRef is absent from passengersSelectedSeats entirely) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertions: Book/Retrieve succeed; selectedOffer.passengerFareBreakdown for the INF paxRef has paxTotalSeatAmount.amount == 0 (or the field/array absent) and no passengerSeats entries; the ADT's paxTotalSeatAmount matches the selected cell's price; totalSelectedSeatsAmount equals only the ADT's seat price, not double-counted for the INF.
Actual Result
All assertions hold. The infant needs no placeholder entry in passengersSelectedSeats: INF paxTotalSeatAmount 0.00 SAR with empty passengerSeats, ADT 60.00 SAR, totalSelectedSeatsAmount 60.00 SAR (once). Fare lines: ADT 993.00 + INF 111.00 = 1104.00 = totalAmount. Unchanged from Rounds 5-6.

View Test Case
Preconditions
AddPassenger completed; GetSeatMap completed and a wheelchair-accessible cell identified by inspecting cellCharacteristics/description text.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap (identify a wheelchair-accessible cell by description/characteristics) -> Book (assign that cell to the relevant passenger) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. Expect Book/Retrieve to succeed with the seat attached like any other paid/free seat; there is no evidenced SSR (special-service-request) field anywhere in the current V2 Book/AddPassenger schema (§2.5/§2.9) to carry a WCHR code alongside the seat, so if Seat map - Seatmap.md's TC-INT-BOOK-014 expectation of a linked SSR flag is correct, that would be an undocumented field this suite has not yet discovered -- treat any SSR-linkage behavior found as a new SPEC.md §2.9 finding, not something to assume exists.
Actual Result
Not executable: the vocabulary (CHARGEABLE_SEAT, LEG_SPACE_SEAT, FRONT_OF_CABIN, SEAT_WITH_BASSINET_FACILITY, BULKHEAD_SEAT, LEFT/RIGHT_SIDE_OF_AIRCRAFT, CENTER_SEAT, AISLE_SEAT, WINDOW, OVER_WING_SEAT_S, EXIT_ROW_SEAT, PREFERRED_SEAT_PREFERENTIAL_SEAT, NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS, NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL) contains no wheelchair designation. Two values are new since Round 6: NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_INFANTS (exit rows) and NOT_ALLOWED_FOR_MEDICAL (exit rows and a few rear rows) - restrictions, not accessibility markers. Not called.
TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-03 - Verify overall cellAvailability and per-passenger seatPriceDetailsByPassenger entries are independently reported, may legitimately differ for the same cell, and are NOT required to list every passenger on the offer.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check each passenger's own availability and pricing agree

Large arrays, objects and long opaque tokens are truncated for report length (marked "__omitted__" / "[truncated]"); the full payload was inspected live. Raw supplier payloads are redacted per SPEC.md §7.14.
View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a multi-passenger offer with a populated seatMapDetails.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> for a sample of cells, compare cellAvailability (overall) against the set of passenger refs actually present in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for that cell -> cross-check each listed passenger's presence against passengersSeatMapAvailability.<paxRef>.<segmentRefId> (the separate top-level per-passenger cellCode allow-list, also confirmed present in the same saved example).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion (structural, not value-equality, and NOT a completeness requirement): a passenger's absence from a cell's seatPriceDetailsByPassenger is EXPECTED and valid whenever that passenger is not eligible for that cell (confirmed pattern: a CHD/INF passenger restricted from a forward/exit cell won't appear there, per this same example's passengersSeatMapAvailability showing PAX3/PAX4 with a much shorter or empty allow-list than PAX1/PAX2). Do NOT assert every passenger must appear per priced cell -- only assert internal consistency: a passenger listed in seatPriceDetailsByPassenger for a cell SHOULD also have that cell's cellCode present in their own passengersSeatMapAvailability entry (if that top-level structure is present in the response). Do not assert cellAvailability == a per-passenger equivalent for all passengers either, since SeatMap QC Execution Checklist.md §11 explicitly notes these may differ legitimately (e.g. a seat blocked for one passenger type but not another).
Actual Result
Internally consistent: 240 passenger-cell price entries (120 x 2), 0 listed for a cell absent from that passenger's allow-list, 0 allow-list codes without a priced cell. GulfAir lists every passenger on every cell, so the "absence is valid" branch could not be exercised (not required). Per-passenger and overall availability DO legitimately differ on one cell: 8E (bassinet seat) is AvailablePaid overall but AvailableFree for both passengers at 0.00 SAR. For context: the CHD passenger is offered every exit-row cell (24 of 24), the already-tracked BUG-09.
TC-SEATMAP-BIZ-04 - Exploratory -- confirm GetSeatMap reflects real-time supplier inventory rather than a cached/stale snapshot.PASS
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map shows live seat availability
Request: Opened the seat map (seat 12C available), booked seat 12C, then opened the same offer again and a brand-new offer
Response: Before: 12C available at 60 SAR. After: 12C gone on both; 179 seats became 178
Expected: Unknown — a live map changes when a seat is taken
Actual: Confirmed live: the change showed at once. A taken seat appears as an empty cell, not as "occupied". No caching headers were sent
Status: PASS
Evidence
Row 12 seat C: AvailablePaid (before) -> NoSeat/null (same-offer #2 and fresh offer); seat cells 179 -> 178; response headers: content-encoding, content-type, correlationid, date, server (no Cache-Control/ETag)

View Test Case
Preconditions
A test environment/mechanism that can independently occupy a seat between the two GetSeatMap calls (may require a second tester/session or coordination with the team -- environment-dependent, same caveat class as TC-BOOK-NEG-09).
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap call #1 (record a specific cell's cellAvailability) -> independently occupy/select that same cell via a separate booking action -> GetSeatMap call #2 (same offer/segment) -> compare the cell's cellAvailability between the two calls.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically; if reliably forceable, expect the cell's cellAvailability to transition (e.g. AvailablePaid -> Occupied) between the two calls, confirming a live supplier round-trip rather than a cached response. If not reliably forceable in this environment, downgrade to logging response timing/headers (e.g. absence of a Cache-Control/ETag suggesting no caching layer) as weaker circumstantial evidence instead.
Actual Result
CONFIRMED live inventory (as in Rounds 11-12). The seat was taken by this session's own booking, and both the same-offer re-read and a fresh-offer seat map dropped it immediately. A taken seat is still not reported as cellAvailability "Occupied": the cell becomes cellCategory "NoSeat" with cellDetails null. Response headers carry a CorrelationId only - no Cache-Control or ETag.
🔁Regression3 passed1 failed
TC-SEATMAP-REG-02 - Verify seatMapDetails.<segment>.{cabinLayoutsByDeck, rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails}}} structure matches the fuller schema captured 2026-08-10, AND flag/tolerate the flat-columns supplier variant (no zones[]/zoneId) confirmed present in a saved example.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map layout matches the documented structure
Request: Compared one live seat map field by field with the project specification
Response: Every documented field is present with the right type; the layout uses the cabin-section style
Expected: The documented fields are all present and correctly typed
Actual: Nothing is missing or wrong, but the response has four fields the specification does not mention (plus the "no seat" category). Kept as a fail for continuity with earlier rounds; the fix is a specification update
Status: FAIL

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetSeatMap completed for a confirmed offer.
Steps
  1. GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response -> schema-diff against SPEC.md §2.7's current field list -> explicitly branch on which cabinLayoutsByDeck shape this supplier returns (zones[].{zoneId,columns} vs. a flat columns[] array) and whether rows[] entries carry zoneId at all, rather than assuming one shape.
Expected Result
Every OTHER key listed in SPEC.md §2.7 (rows[].{rowNumber,deck,cells[].{cellCategory,column,cellDetails.{cellID,cellCode,cellAvailability,name,description,seatPriceDetails,seatPriceDetailsByPassenger,cellCharacteristics}}}) is present and correctly typed. The cabinLayoutsByDeck/zoneId shape is now confirmed to vary by supplier -- do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking zones[]/zoneId if it instead provides the flat columns[] array (AirArabia-confirmed variant); do NOT hard-fail a response for lacking the flat columns[] array if it instead provides zones[]/zoneId. Treat presence of at least one of the two shapes as passing, and log which shape each supplier uses.
Actual Result
Every documented key is present and correctly typed: cabinLayoutsByDeck.Main.zones[].{zoneId,columns,cabinClass}, rows[].{rowNumber,deck,zoneId,cells[]}, cellDetails.{cellID,cellCode,cellAvailability,name,description,seatPriceDetails,seatPriceDetailsByPassenger,cellCharacteristics}. GulfAir uses the zones[]/zoneId shape and rows[] carry zoneId. The response also carries 4 fields SPEC.md 2.7 does not list (isFareCheckRequired, passengersSeatMapAvailability, birthDate, documentNumber) and a NoSeat cellCategory - the same schema drift flagged in every prior round, so kept FAIL for continuity; nothing is missing or mistyped.

View Test Case
Preconditions
TC-BOOK-POS-03 (or the equivalent BookAfterHold-branch flow) completed with a seat selected; the environment/supplier ticketing process allowed to run to completion (may require a wait or a supplier-specific trigger).
Steps
  1. Book (seat selected) -> Retrieve #1 (record passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats) -> wait for ticketing to complete (tickets[].ticketStatus transitions, ticketingDate populated) -> Retrieve #2 -> compare seat-related fields between #1 and #2.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats/totalSelectedSeatsAmount in Retrieve #2 are identical to Retrieve #1 -- the seat assignment does not disappear or change once ticketing completes.
Actual Result
The seat-related fields are byte-for-byte identical across both Retrieves. GulfAir tickets synchronously at Book time (ticket number and ticketingDate exist from the first Retrieve), so no Booked-to-ticketed transition can be observed on this supplier - best-effort per the test's own timing note; the persistence assertion holds. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.

View Test Case
Preconditions
A valid AddPassenger-derived ResponseId/selectedOfferId pair; a second supplier/credentialsSelector pair available for the cross-tenant variant.
Steps
  1. Run (1) with a corrupted x-api-key. Run (2) with a corrupted Client-Id. Run (3) with valid headers but a different supplier/credentialsSelector than the one used to establish this ResponseId/selectedOfferId.
Expected Result
All three rejected (exact status/error shape UNKNOWN, confirm live and reuse whatever envelope the same three checks produce on other endpoints, §7.14, for consistency).
Actual Result
Two of the three checks pass cleanly; the third half-passes. A wrong supplier is rejected (400), but switching only credentialsSelector to another valid one for the same supplier (GulfAir/UAE) is NOT rejected: GetSeatMap returns the complete seat map for an offer created under KSA. credentialsSelector is still not enforced as an authorization boundary on GetSeatMap (BUG-17, 3rd round in a row).

View Test Case
Preconditions
Bundle code obtained from GetOfferBundles; ancillary code obtained from GetAncillary; cellCode/cellId obtained from GetSeatMap -- all for the same offer/passenger chain.
Steps
  1. GetOfferBundles (record bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetAncillary (record ancillary code) -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId) -> FareCheck -> Book (submit all three fields populated together).
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live. The collection's current saved Book example carries only passengersSelectedSeats active, with selectedBundles/PassengersSelectedAncillaries left commented out -- this combination has not been directly evidenced as accepted. Record whichever outcome occurs (accepted with all three reflected in the response, partially accepted, or rejected) as the new ground truth.
Actual Result
Not executable for GulfAir: it exposes no bundle capability on any sampled offer, so the bundle half of the combination cannot be built. Not called - no request was sent for this case. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.
TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-INT-04 - Determine SeatAfterHold's actual position in the Hold-branch chain by attempting it at three candidate points and comparing outcomes.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Find where in the hold process adding a seat is allowed
Request: Tried adding a seat at three points: right after the hold, after re-pricing the hold, and after final booking
Response: Refused with the same message at all three points; re-pricing is also not supported for this airline; final booking worked
Expected: Unknown — record which point accepts it and whether the seat shows in the final booking
Actual: Cannot be answered for this airline: the refusal does not depend on the point, and no booking ended with a seat. New finding: re-pricing a hold is also unavailable
Status: FAIL
Evidence
A: SAH 409, PnrReprice 409, BookAfterHold 200 (OWRLBM ticket 722136997158); B: PnrReprice 409, SAH 409, BookAfterHold 200 (OODBGD); C: PnrReprice 409, BookAfterHold 200 (OWZVVL), SAH 409; all Retrieve pSS {}

View Test Case
Preconditions
Three independent Hold calls (or one Hold reused up to the branch point, if the API tolerates repeated FareConfirmAfterHold calls) for the same supplier/credentialsSelector.
Steps
  1. Chain A: Hold -> SeatAfterHold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain B: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve. Chain C: Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold -> Retrieve. Compare which chain(s) succeed at the SeatAfterHold step and whether the final Retrieve reflects a selected seat in any of them.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- resolve empirically. Record which candidate position(s) SeatAfterHold accepts without erroring, and whether the resulting Retrieve response shows passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11) for that chain. If more than one position succeeds without erroring, that itself is a finding worth reporting (an under-constrained endpoint), not assumed to be intentional flexibility.
Actual Result
Not resolvable for GulfAir. SeatAfterHold rejects at every position with the identical supplier-level 409, so the outcome is not position-dependent (BUG-03), and no chain ends with a seat. New: FareConfirmAfterHold is also rejected for GulfAir (409 OperationNotSupported), so positions B and C could not even be reached the way the chain intends. Ground truth for the flow position stays UNKNOWN.

View Test Case
Preconditions
GetOfferBundles completed (bundle code + JourneyKey recorded); GetSeatMap completed (cellCode/cellId recorded for a segment within the same journey as the chosen bundle).
Steps
  1. GetOfferBundles (record JourneyKey/bundle code) -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellId for a segment belonging to that JourneyKey) -> Book (submit both selectedBundles and passengersSelectedSeats together, matching journey) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: Book succeeds; response reflects both the bundle and the seat without either overriding the other's pricing (selectedOffer.priceDetails carries both a bundle-inclusive component and totalSelectedSeatsAmount, not double-counted or dropped).
Actual Result
Not executable for GulfAir - no bundle capability on any sampled offer, so no JourneyKey/bundle code exists to cross-check against a seat's segmentRefId. Not called. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Each candidate supplier confirmed SeatMap-capable live (isSeatMapRequired observed true on at least one real offer) before including it in this run.
Steps
  1. For each of the 3+ chosen suppliers: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap -> snapshot the full response schema (key names/types/nesting, not values).
Expected Result
Automatable assertion: every supplier's GetSeatMap response conforms to the identical schema documented in SPEC.md §2.7 (same top-level keys, same seatMapDetails/cellDetails nesting) regardless of the supplier's native protocol -- differences are limited to data values (cellCode ranges, characteristics, pricing), never to the shape itself. A supplier whose response requires a materially different assertion path is a normalization defect in the supplier-adapter layer (§1.3), not an acceptable per-supplier variation.
Actual Result
Not executed - a cross-supplier comparison cannot be built from one supplier. GulfAir's own response shape was checked on 34 segments and is stable (see VAL-10, VAL-11, REG-02). Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.
TC-SEATMAP-INT-03 - Capability-matrix sweep -- run GetSeatMap against every supplier confirmed or plausibly SeatMap-capable per SPEC.md §4.6, and record pass/fail per supplier.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Check the seat map for every airline that offers it
Request: Would need a sweep of every airline in the roster; only GulfAir was in scope
Response: GulfAir: 34 of 34 flights returned a populated seat map
Expected: Every capable airline works and the rest fail politely
Actual: Blocked by scope. GulfAir's row is re-confirmed; seat maps are empty for flights after about early August 2027
Status: BLOCKED
Evidence
GulfAir/KSA: 34 of 34 sampled segments returned a populated seatMapDetails; departures from 2027-08-03 returned an empty seatMapDetails (0 rows)
View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier roster and capability status pulled from SPEC.md §4.5/§4.6 for each run.
Steps
  1. For each supplier in scope: run the §4.7 capability-confirmation procedure -> if SeatMap-capable (or Unknown/Conditional, per §4.4-style caution), run GetSeatMap -> record HTTP status and whether seatMapDetails is populated.
Expected Result
Every confirmed-capable supplier's GetSeatMap call succeeds with a populated seatMapDetails; every explicitly-not-capable supplier is expected to fail gracefully (cross-ref TC-SEATMAP-NEG-01's pattern) rather than silently succeed with an empty response. Build/maintain the resulting per-supplier pass/fail table as a living artifact alongside SPEC.md §4.6.
Actual Result
Not executed as a sweep. GulfAir/KSA is confirmed SeatMap-supported for the 7th round (with the caveat that seat maps are empty for departures after about early August 2027, and Search returns no offers after about mid-July 2027). No other supplier was called. Unchanged from Rounds 1-6.

Review SPEC.md §1.5/§1.8 (static, hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id sent by THIS layer to the caller; supplier-side credentials are a separate, server-side-only concern not exposed in any request/response this suite can observe) and the PRD's §7 Non-Functional Requirements (file-only ApiResponse/SLF4J logger, correlation-ID tracing) for what actually governs supplier-auth and logging.
Expected Result
This case does not assert a pass/fail against the live API. It documents that: (a) User Story AC8's "securely authenticates with airline supplier APIs" describes THIS system's outbound credential handling toward suppliers -- a server-side/config concern, confirmable only via a backend credential-storage/config audit or the automation framework's own code review (PRD §7's Gap #1 already flags this as hardcoded tech debt), not via any request this Postman-collection-driven suite can send; (b) AC9's "provides logging" is confirmable only via log/observability review (PRD §7's ApiResponse logger, correlation-ID tracing), not via API response inspection. TC-SEATMAP-NEG-05 covers AC9's "handles errors gracefully" half, which IS API-observable.
Actual Result
Documented as specified; SPEC.md 1.5 and 1.8 and NDC_PRD.md Gap #1 (hardcoded x-api-key/Client-Id) re-checked and still say the same. AC8/AC9 must not be marked covered by API tests without the paired backend/config/log audit. Unchanged from Rounds 1-12.

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-49 (capability confirmation per §4.7, variable reset per §6.1). Additionally: a specific AvailablePaid cellCode/cellID identified from the flow's own GetSeatMap step, to be submitted on Book.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID; capture getSeatMapOfferId/getSeatMapResponceID) -> FareCheck (if isFareCheckRequired) -> Book (send ResponseId=getSeatMapResponceID, selectedOfferId=getSeatMapOfferId, passengersSelectedSeats populated with the recorded cellCode/cellID) -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
Per-family state check (§6.3 Family A) plus the new seat-specific checks: Book/Retrieve both echo passengersSelectedSeats matching the selection; selectedOffer.priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount is non-zero and (per TC-BOOK-BIZ-04) reconciles into totalAmount.
Actual Result
Book and Retrieve both echo the two seats (14C, 14D) and priceDetails.totalSelectedSeatsAmount = 120.00 reconciles into totalAmount 1730.00 (849 + 761 + 0 + 120) on both. But the Retrieve response is internally inconsistent for a multi-seat booking: the passenger line shows paxTotalSeatAmount 60.00 while its passengerSeats hold two 60.00 seats (120.00), and paxTotalAmount 1670.00 (= 849 + 761 + 60) does not equal the Book response's 1730.00 or the offer total, so the per-passenger totals no longer sum to totalAmount. It reproduced on a second Retrieve and on the two-passenger round trip (paxTotalSeatAmount 60 for seats worth 100 each, per-passenger totals summing to 3340 against 3420). Round 6's round-trip Retrieve was consistent (240 for two 120 seats), so this is a new defect (BUG-18).
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01 - Verify Search-to-Retrieve completes with a selected seat when SeatAfterHold is called immediately after Hold, before FareConfirmAfterHold.FAIL
Endpoint Name: Hold, add a seat straight away, re-price, book, read back
Request: Held a booking (Bahrain to Jeddah, 20 May 2027) and tried to add a seat straight after the hold, then continued to the end for information
Response: Adding the seat was refused; re-pricing was refused; the final booking (OWRLBM) went through with no seat
Expected: Unknown — the seat should be accepted if this is the right order
Actual: Fails at the add-seat step because this airline is not supported (BUG-03). The remaining steps were still run to see what would happen
Status: FAIL

SAH 409 OperationNotSupported "GulfAir does not exist(s)"; PnrReprice 409; BookAfterHold 200 pnr OWRLBM; Retrieve pSS {}

View Test Case
Preconditions
Supplier/credentialsSelector confirmed live-capable for Hold (§4.7). Collection variables reset (§6.1). Tester aware this flow's very structure is unconfirmed -- run TC-SEATAFTERHOLD-INT-04 first if not already done.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold (capture pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, holdExpirationDate) -> SeatAfterHold (submit supplier, credentialsSelector, pnr, gdsPNR, bookingToken, surName -- per §2.7a's documented-but-unconfirmed body) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design. If this chain position is correct, expect SeatAfterHold to succeed and the final Retrieve to show passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats/totalSelectedSeats populated (§2.11), with FareConfirmAfterHold's re-priced total reflecting the added seat cost. If this is the wrong chain position, expect SeatAfterHold or a later step to reject.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-03). The chain fails at the SeatAfterHold hop: GulfAir is rejected outright (409 OperationNotSupported). It was continued to the end for information: FareConfirmAfterHold is also unsupported for GulfAir (409), BookAfterHold finalizes the booking and the final Retrieve carries no seat.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-02 - Verify Search-to-Retrieve completes with a selected seat when SeatAfterHold is called after FareConfirmAfterHold, before BookAfterHold.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Hold, re-price, add a seat, book, read back
Request: Held a booking (Bahrain to Dammam, 21 May 2027), tried to re-price it, then to add a seat, then booked and read it back
Response: Re-pricing refused; adding the seat refused; the final booking (OODBGD) went through with no seat

Preconditions
Same as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> Hold -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> SeatAfterHold (submit pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken/surName, unchanged since Hold) -> BookAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN by design -- same expected-outcome logic as FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01, but testing whether re-pricing (FareConfirmAfterHold) must happen before or after the seat is attached.
Actual Result
Blocked. The chain cannot be built as designed: its third step (FareConfirmAfterHold) is rejected for GulfAir, and SeatAfterHold is rejected at supplier level regardless of position, so the before/after-re-pricing question cannot be answered. Executed to the end this round (Rounds 1-6 reasoned this one blocked without running it).
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-03 - Verify a selected seat can still be attached via SeatAfterHold after BookAfterHold has already finalized the booking.BLOCKED
Endpoint Name: Hold, re-price, book, then add a seat, read back
Request: Held a booking (Bahrain to Riyadh, 25 May 2027), tried to re-price it, booked it, then tried to add a seat
Response: Re-pricing refused; the booking (OWZVVL) went through; adding a seat afterwards was refused; no seat on the read-back
Expected: Unknown — refused if seats must be chosen before booking, accepted otherwise
Actual: Blocked: the same airline-level refusal, so it says nothing about whether seats can be added after booking
Status: BLOCKED

Expected Result

View Test Case
Preconditions
Same preconditions as the existing FLOW-V2-50, plus a recorded cellCode/cellID from this flow's own GetSeatMap step.
Steps
  1. Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (record cellCode/cellID) -> FareCheck (if required) -> Hold (attempt to also submit passengersSelectedSeats on this Hold call, mirroring Book's shape) -> FareConfirmAfterHold -> Retrieve.
Expected Result
UNKNOWN -- confirm live whether Hold silently ignores an unrecognized passengersSelectedSeats field, rejects the request outright for an unexpected field, or (surprisingly) accepts it. SPEC.md §2.10/§1.10-item6 currently documents this field as absent from Hold's contract based on the saved example alone, not a live-confirmed rejection -- this case supplies that live confirmation. Regardless of outcome, the flow's Retrieve step should be checked for whether passengersSelectedSeats/passengerSeats appear at all without a SeatAfterHold call having been made.
Actual Result
STILL REPRODUCES (BUG-08). Hold does not ignore or reject the field: it accepts it, prices the seat into the held offer (totalSelectedSeatsAmount 60.00) and Retrieve shows the seat on the OnHold booking, all without any SeatAfterHold call. This contradicts SPEC.md 1.10 item 6 / 2.10, which describe Hold as having no seat field. New: FareConfirmAfterHold (PnrReprice) is rejected for GulfAir with 409 OperationNotSupported, so the flow cannot reach its documented fourth step.
FLOW-V2-CANDIDATE-SM-HOLD-01-NEG - Validate SeatAfterHold rejects a pnr/gdsPNR/bookingToken triple carried over from a different, unrelated Hold call earlier in the same test session.BLOCKED

Expected: Refused because the details belong to another hold
Actual: Blocked: a stale set of details cannot be told apart from a correct one while every request is refused
Status: BLOCKED
